sites.rationale: L2 explicitly names eAE1 position 557 as the Myc-tag insertion site within the third extracellular loop of kAE1; L1 independently corroborates an HA tag at the identical eAE1 position 557 in a separate construct. Python verification confirms residue 557 = V and residue 558 = L in the canonical 911-aa sequence, and that position 557 lies within the authoritative EC3 span 542–569, ≥16 residues from either TM boundary. No cysteine or N-glycosylation sequon (NxS/T) is present in EC3, and the loop is 28 residues long, providing ample space for a ~15–23 aa insert. Full-length kAE1 constructs (pcDNA3.1-kAE1 WT-Myc and pcDNA3.1-kAE1 WT-HA) carrying a Myc or HA epitope tag at position 557 in eAE1 numbering, located in the third extracellular loop (EC3) of the membrane domain. Constructs were expressed in mammalian cells and used for expression and functional studies of SLC4A1 trafficking variants. L1 (PMC12959882) independently confirms an HA tag at the same eAE1 position 557 in a lentiviral kAE1 construct used for expression studies. [validation: surface_only; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The kAE1-Myc protein has a Myc tag at position 557 in the third extracellular loop of the kAE1 protein, while the kAE1-HA protein has a HA tag at the C-terminus of the kAE1 protein. pcDNA3.1-kAE1 WT-Myc and pcDNA3.1-kAE1 WT-HA were used as templates for generation of pcDNA3.1-kAE1 T444N-Myc and pcDNA3.1-kAE1 T444N-HA by site-directed mutagenesis method using specific primers ( SLC4A1 -T444N forward: 5′-GGAGCTGCTGATCTCCAATGCAGTGCAGGGCATTC-3′; SLC4A1 -T444N reverse: 5′-GAATGCCCTGCACTGCATTGGAGATCAGCAGCTCC-3′) and Pfx DNA polymerase (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA), as described previously [ 22 ].

sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface biotinylation followed by immunoblot detected V5-tagged eAE1 at the cell surface of HEK293 cells, confirming correct trafficking and surface display. Anion transport function of the V5-tagged construct is NOT MEASURED in the cited work.
sites.rationale: L3 provides the flanking peptide YNVL[V5]MVPK for the eAE1 EL3 construct; Python sequence search locates YNVL at eAE1 555–558 and MVPK at 559–562, unambiguously placing the V5 insertion after residue 558 (L558, residue_after = M559). Position 558 lies within the authoritative EC3 span 542–569, ≥17 residues from TM5 (ends 541) and ≥12 from TM6 (starts 570). EC3 contains no cysteines and no N-glycosylation sequons, and the 28-residue loop accommodates a short epitope tag without steric conflict. L4 independently confirms surface biotinylation of this same V5-tagged eAE1 construct. Full-length human eAE1 with a V5 tag inserted into EL3 (residues 555–576) was expressed in HEK293 cells. The flanking peptide reported in L3 is YNVL–[V5]–MVPK, where YNVL = eAE1 555–558 and MVPK = eAE1 559–562, pinning the insertion junction to after residue 558 (L). Surface display was confirmed by surface biotinylation and immunoblot (L4). [validation: surface_only; position: inferred; source: paper; cited_tag_residue: 558; entailment_verified: True]

literature_notes: Four ledger lines were evaluated. L1 and L2 both pin an HA or Myc tag to eAE1 position 557 in the third extracellular loop (EC3, 542–569); they support the same junction (insert_after_residue=557) and are consolidated into Site 1, with L2 as the primary citation because it provides more experimental detail. L3 pins a V5 tag to the adjacent junction after residue 558 via an explicit flanking-peptide readout; L4 confirms surface display of the same construct and is treated as corroborating evidence for Site 2. Both sites are in EC3, which is the only loop long enough (28 residues) to carry a short epitope tag comfortably; all other extracellular spans in SLC4A1 are 1–15 residues (EC1 14 aa, EC2 15 aa, EC4 36 aa, EC5 1 aa, EC6 1 aa, EC7 7 aa). EC4 (625–660, 36 aa) has no ledger-supported insertion and was not proposed. No ledger line supports any terminal tag (the N-terminus is intracellular and the C-terminus is intracellular), so no terminal sites are reported.
